title: CSS3D Caffeine Molecule
prompt:
Use Three.js's CSS3DRenderer to display a caffeine molecule: represent 24 atoms with CSS3DSprite (the elements may be div elements containing symbols), and represent chemical bonds with CSS3DObject (long, thin div elements); support clicking atoms to view an information panel and automatic rotation.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
import { CSS3DRenderer, CSS3DObject, CSS3DSprite } from 'three/addons/renderers/CSS3DRenderer.js';
</script>

[Structure]
(1) Arrange 24 atoms according to caffeine's actual bonding structure (the C/H/N/O counts must match the molecular formula C8H10N4O2), together with the corresponding covalent bonds (the number of bonds and geometry only need to be reasonable; bondCount is the number of bond objects in the scene).
(2) Atom labels: for example, "C1", "N1", etc., using the same naming scheme as __3D_STATE__.selectedAtom.
(3) Clicking an atom: highlight it and update the information panel (element name, index, etc.); selectedAtom must be a string, and may be null or "" when no atom is selected.
(4) id="autoRotate": a checkbox that controls OrbitControls.autoRotate.

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  atomCount: number,          // Always 24
  bondCount: number,          // Number of bonds (provide the expected value in an implementation comment)
  selectedAtom: string | null,
  autoRotate: boolean,
  moleculeName: string          // Always "caffeine" or "Caffeine"
}

[Evaluation Support (Required, for StateProbe)]
(5) window.__STATEPROBE_selectAtom__(label: string | null): programmatically select an atom, equivalent to clicking it; pass null or an empty string to clear the selection.

Output a single HTML file that runs when opened directly in a browser.
